literal: Empress Dowager Ling subtly detected it.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling subtly detected it.

literal: In autumn of the fifth year of Zhengguang Ling told Ming and the ministers she wished to leave the world for Xianju Temple on Mount Song and to shave her own head.
idiomatic: In autumn of the fifth year of Zhengguang Ling told Ming and the ministers she wished to leave the world for Xianju Temple on Mount Song and to shave her own head.

literal: The emperor and ministers were greatly afraid and kowtowed weeping.
idiomatic: The emperor and ministers were greatly afraid and kowtowed weeping.

literal: They then secretly plotted with the dowager against him.
idiomatic: They then secretly plotted with the dowager against him.

literal: They then wept before Cha and told of the dowager's wish to leave the world and her fearful heart.
idiomatic: They then wept before Cha and told of the dowager's wish to leave the world and her fearful heart.

literal: Cha then urged the emperor to follow the dowager's wish.
idiomatic: Cha then urged the emperor to follow the dowager's wish.

literal: Then the dowager often held court at Xianyang; the two palaces were no longer barred.
idiomatic: Then the dowager often held court at Xianyang; the two palaces were no longer barred.

literal: His kinsman Yuan Faseng was raised to Governor of Xu Province; Faseng held the province and rebelled.
idiomatic: His kinsman Yuan Faseng was raised to Governor of Xu Province; Faseng held the province and rebelled.

literal: Ling spoke of it repeatedly; Cha was deeply ashamed.
idiomatic: Ling spoke of it repeatedly; Cha was deeply ashamed.

literal: Prime Minister Prince of Gaoyang Yong, though higher in rank than Cha, greatly feared him.
idiomatic: Prime Minister Prince of Gaoyang Yong, though higher in rank than Cha, greatly feared him.

literal: When the dowager and emperor toured the Luo River they then visited Yong's residence and settled the plan against Cha.
idiomatic: When the dowager and emperor toured the Luo River they then visited Yong's residence and settled the plan against Cha.

literal: Later Yong followed the emperor to audience with the dowager and advanced the argument that Cha father and son held excessive power.
idiomatic: Later Yong followed the emperor to audience with the dowager and advanced the argument that Cha father and son held excessive power.

literal: The dowager said: "So it is.
idiomatic: The dowager said: "So it is.

literal: If Lord Yuan is loyal to the court, why does he not leave command of the guards and assist in government with his other offices?
idiomatic: If Lord Yuan is loyal to the court, why does he not leave command of the guards and assist in government with his other offices?

literal: " Cha heard and was greatly afraid; he removed his cap and begged release.
idiomatic: " Cha heard and was greatly afraid. He removed his cap and begged release.

literal: Cha was then made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, Director of the Masters of Writing, Palace Attendant, and Commander of the Left and Right.
idiomatic: Cha was then made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, Director of the Masters of Writing, Palace Attendant, and Commander of the Left and Right.

literal: Though Cha had lost military power he still held overall charge inside and outside and did not fear dismissal.
idiomatic: Though Cha had lost military power he still held overall charge inside and outside and did not fear dismissal.

literal: Also eunuchs Zhang Jingsong, Liu Siyi, Tun Hongchang, and Fu Jing plotted to depose Cha.
idiomatic: Also eunuchs Zhang Jingsong, Liu Siyi, Tun Hongchang, and Fu Jing plotted to depose Cha.

literal: Song, because the emperor's consort Pan Wailian was favored, told Yun that Yuan Cha wished to harm her.
idiomatic: Song, because the emperor's consort Pan Wailian was favored, told Yun that Yuan Cha wished to harm her.

literal: The consort wept and told the emperor: "Cha does not only wish to kill me—he will also harm Your Majesty.
idiomatic: The consort wept and told the emperor: "Cha does not only wish to kill me—he will also harm Your Majesty.

literal: " The emperor believed it.
idiomatic: " The emperor believed it.

literal: Later when Cha lodged outside they removed his Palace Attendant post.
idiomatic: Later when Cha lodged outside they removed his Palace Attendant post.

literal: At dawn he wished to enter the palace; the gatekeepers would not admit him.
idiomatic: At dawn he wished to enter the palace; the gatekeepers would not admit him.

literal: Soon he was struck from the rolls.
idiomatic: Soon he was struck from the rolls.

literal: At first Prince of Xianyang Xi was executed for treason; his son Shu, Liang enfeoffed as Prince of Ye.
idiomatic: At first Prince of Xianyang Xi was executed for treason; his son Shu, Liang enfeoffed as Prince of Ye.

literal: After Faseng rebelled Shu sent a letter to the hundred officials exposing Cha's crimes, saying: "Cha's original name is Yecha; his younger brother Luo's true name is Luosha.
idiomatic: After Faseng rebelled Shu sent a letter to the hundred officials exposing Cha's crimes, saying: "Cha's original name is Yecha; his younger brother Luo's true name is Luosha.

literal: Yecha and Luosha—these demons devour men; unless you meet a black wind you fall like blown leaves.
idiomatic: Yecha and Luosha—these demons devour men. Unless you meet a black wind you fall like blown leaves.

literal: Alas, Wei territory!
idiomatic: Alas, Wei territory!

literal: Keep far from these two disasters.
idiomatic: Keep far from these two disasters.

literal: Evil tree, stolen spring—do not rest, do not drink; a name surpassing the owl—do not enter, do not become.
idiomatic: Evil tree, stolen spring—do not rest, do not drink; a name surpassing the owl—do not enter, do not become.

literal: How much more when brothers bear such names, showing they can devour—exposed so long, one finally believes the saying.
idiomatic: How much more when brothers bear such names, showing they can devour—exposed so long, one finally believes the saying.

literal: " Cha was hated near and far like this.
idiomatic: " Cha was hated near and far like this.

literal: Later Ling said to attendants: "Liu Teng and Yuan Cha once begged me for an iron certificate, hoping not to die; I relied on not giving it.
idiomatic: Later Ling said to attendants: "Liu Teng and Yuan Cha once begged me for an iron certificate, hoping not to die. I relied on not giving it.

literal: " Central Secretariat Attendant Han Zishun replied: "Your servant hears that killing and sparing do not depend on giving or not.
idiomatic: " Central Secretariat Attendant Han Zishun replied: "Your servant hears that killing and sparing do not depend on giving or not.

literal: Though Your Majesty did not give then, why not kill today?
idiomatic: Though Your Majesty did not give then, why not kill today?

literal: " Ling was displeased.
idiomatic: " Ling was displeased.

literal: Before long someone reported that Cha and his younger brother Zhao plotted rebellion.
idiomatic: Before long someone reported that Cha and his younger brother Zhao plotted rebellion.

literal: First he sent his cousin Hongye to lead surrendered households of the six garrisons to rebel at Ding Province;
idiomatic: First he sent his cousin Hongye to lead surrendered households of the six garrisons to rebel at Ding Province;

literal: Cha ordered Gou of Luyang and various tribes to harass Yique; Cha and his brothers were inside accomplices—the day was set; they obtained his handwriting.
idiomatic: Cha ordered Gou of Luyang and various tribes to harass Yique. Cha and his brothers were inside accomplices—the day was set; they obtained his handwriting.

literal: Ling, because he was her sister's husband, could not bear to decide at once.
idiomatic: Ling, because he was her sister's husband, could not bear to decide at once.

literal: The ministers pressed without cease; Ming also spoke; the dowager then assented.
idiomatic: The ministers pressed without cease; Ming also spoke; the dowager then assented.

literal: Then Cha and his younger brother Zhao were granted death at home.
idiomatic: Then Cha and his younger brother Zhao were granted death at home.

literal: The dowager still because of her sister posthumously restored him Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: The dowager still because of her sister posthumously restored him Director of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Ji Province.

literal: Cha's son Shu was Secretariat Gentleman.
idiomatic: Cha's son Shu was Secretariat Gentleman.

literal: After Cha died he fled to Liang and rose to Grand General Conquering the North and Governor of Qing and Ji Provinces.
idiomatic: After Cha died he fled to Liang and rose to Grand General Conquering the North and Governor of Qing and Ji Provinces.

literal: His son Shan, also called Shanshan.
idiomatic: His son Shan, also called Shanshan.

literal: Young he followed his father to the south; fond of learning, versed in the Five Classics, especially skilled in the Zuo Commentary.
idiomatic: Young he followed his father to the south. Fond of learning, he was versed in the Five Classics and especially skilled in the Zuo Commentary.

literal: In the turmoil of Hou Jing Shan returned to Zhou; Emperor Wu greatly honored him, made him Tutor of the Crown Prince's Palace, enfeoffed Duke of Jiangyang, and often lectured on the classics to the crown prince.
idiomatic: In the turmoil of Hou Jing Shan returned to Zhou. Emperor Wu greatly honored him, made him Tutor of the Crown Prince's Palace, enfeoffed Duke of Jiangyang, and often lectured on the classics to the crown prince.

literal: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat; whatever he memorialized, the tone rose and fell, and watchers fixed their eyes on him.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Sui Kaihuang he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat. Whatever he memorialized, the tone rose and fell, and watchers fixed their eyes on him.

literal: Chen envoy Yuan Ya came on embassy; the emperor ordered Shan to go to the lodge to receive the letter.
idiomatic: Chen envoy Yuan Ya came on embassy; the emperor ordered Shan to go to the lodge to receive the letter.

literal: Ya went out the door without bowing.
idiomatic: Ya went out the door without bowing.

literal: Shan argued that by old custom there was a bowing rite; Ya could not answer.
idiomatic: Shan argued that by old custom there was a bowing rite; Ya could not answer.

literal: He then bowed and left with the rite complete.
idiomatic: He then bowed and left with the rite complete.

literal: Later he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Academy.
idiomatic: Later he was transferred to Director of the Imperial Academy.

literal: The emperor once came in person to the libation ceremony and ordered Shan to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety; he then set forth the meaning and also offered remonstrance.
idiomatic: The emperor once came in person to the libation ceremony and ordered Shan to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety. He then set forth the meaning and also offered remonstrance.

literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "Hearing Jiangyang's discourse has renewed my heart.
idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "Hearing Jiangyang's discourse has renewed my heart.

literal: " He was given a hundred bolts of silk and one suit of clothes.
idiomatic: " He was given a hundred bolts of silk and one suit of clothes.

literal: Shan's breadth was below He Tuo, yet by graceful bearing he was pleasing to behold, his voice clear—thus later scholars looked up to him.
idiomatic: Shan's breadth was below He Tuo, yet by graceful bearing he was pleasing to behold, his voice clear—thus later scholars looked up to him.

literal: Tuo always nursed resentment and wished to humble Shan; he therefore lectured on the Spring and Autumn.
idiomatic: Tuo always nursed resentment and wished to humble Shan; he therefore lectured on the Spring and Autumn.

literal: When the topic was first announced all the Confucians gathered; Shan privately told Tuo: "Reputation is already settled—please do not press me hard.
idiomatic: When the topic was first announced all the Confucians gathered. Shan privately told Tuo: "Reputation is already settled—please do not press me hard.

literal: " Tuo agreed.
idiomatic: " Tuo agreed.

literal: When they came to the lecture hall Tuo then cited obscure points from antiquity to challenge Shan; he often could not answer.
idiomatic: When they came to the lecture hall Tuo then cited obscure points from antiquity to challenge Shan; he often could not answer.

literal: From this the two had a rift.
idiomatic: From this the two had a rift.

literal: Shan, because Gao Feng had the makings of a prime minister, once told the emperor: "Yang Su is coarse, Su Wei timid, Yuan Zhou and Yuan Min are like ducks.
idiomatic: Shan, because Gao Feng had the makings of a prime minister, once told the emperor: "Yang Su is coarse, Su Wei timid, Yuan Zhou and Yuan Min are like ducks.

literal: He alone to whom the altars may be entrusted is Gao Feng.
idiomatic: He alone to whom the altars may be entrusted is Gao Feng.

literal: " The emperor at first agreed.
idiomatic: " The emperor at first agreed.

literal: When Feng was punished the emperor took Shan's words as lobbying for Feng and blamed him deeply.
idiomatic: When Feng was punished the emperor took Shan's words as lobbying for Feng and blamed him deeply.

literal: Shan grew anxious and fearful; he had long suffered from wasting thirst, and now fell ill and died suddenly.
idiomatic: Shan grew anxious and fearful. He had long suffered from wasting thirst, and now fell ill and died suddenly.

literal: Cha's younger brother Luo, styled Zhonggang.
idiomatic: Cha's younger brother Luo, styled Zhonggang.

literal: Though father and brothers were noble and flourishing he humbled himself in receiving others.
idiomatic: Though father and brothers were noble and flourishing he humbled himself in receiving others.

literal: He rose repeatedly to Governor of Qing Province.
idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Governor of Qing Province.

literal: When Cha held court and sole power Luo's fame tilted the four seas; at the time men of talent and name such as Wang Yuanjing, Xing Zicai, and Ji Jiang were all his guests and traveled with him in Qing.
idiomatic: When Cha held court and sole power Luo's fame tilted the four seas. At the time men of talent and name such as Wang Yuanjing, Xing Zicai, and Ji Jiang were all his guests and traveled with him in Qing.

literal: Leaving office he entered as Defender of Integrity.
idiomatic: Leaving office he entered as Defender of Integrity.

literal: After Cha died Luo took Cha's wife; men of the time reviled it, some saying it was a plan to save his life.
idiomatic: After Cha died Luo took Cha's wife; men of the time reviled it, some saying it was a plan to save his life.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu he held Director of the Masters of Writing, Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, and Governor of Liang Province.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he held Director of the Masters of Writing, Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, and Governor of Liang Province.

literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing Liang sent generals to press the siege; Luo surrendered the province and was enfeoffed Prince of Nanjun.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiaojing Liang sent generals to press the siege. Luo surrendered the province and was enfeoffed Prince of Nanjun.

literal: When Hou Jing declared himself independent he made Luo Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes and Director of the Masters of Writing, changed his fief to Prince of Jiangyang.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing declared himself independent he made Luo Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes and Director of the Masters of Writing, and changed his fief to Prince of Jiangyang.

literal: When Liang Emperor Yuan destroyed Jing, Zhou Emperor Wen sought Luo and he was able to return.
idiomatic: When Liang Emperor Yuan destroyed Jing, Zhou Emperor Wen sought Luo and he was able to return.

literal: He was made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, Palace Attendant, Junior Preceptor, and inherited as Prince of Jiangyang.
idiomatic: He was made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes, Palace Attendant, Junior Preceptor, and inherited as Prince of Jiangyang.

literal: Shu's son Shanshan, following later, entered the pass from the south; Luo then returned the title to Shanshan and Luo was changed to Duke of Gudao.
idiomatic: Shu's son Shanshan, following later, entered the pass from the south. Luo then returned the title to Shanshan and Luo was changed to Duke of Gudao.

literal: Luo's younger brother Shuang, styled Jingzhe.
idiomatic: Luo's younger brother Shuang, styled Jingzhe.

literal: Clever and alert from youth; he held Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Robe.
idiomatic: Clever and alert from youth, he held Attendant of the Yellow Gate and Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Seal and Purple Robe.

literal: He died; posthumous title Yi.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Yi.

literal: Shuang's younger brother Man served Qi and rose to Acting Director of Revenue and acting Governor of Ying Province.
idiomatic: Shuang's younger brother Man served Qi and rose to Acting Director of Revenue and acting Governor of Ying Province.

literal: He was impeached by the Left Director for not wearing mourning for his stepmother.
idiomatic: He was impeached by the Left Director for not wearing mourning for his stepmother.

literal: Later he was made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: Later he was made Commissioner with the Same Ceremony as the Three Dukes.

literal: In the tenth year of Qi Tianbao the Yuan clan was greatly slaughtered.
idiomatic: In the tenth year of Qi Tianbao the Yuan clan was greatly slaughtered.

literal: Emperor Zhao's Yuan empress was Man's daughter; she pleaded bitterly and bought herself back from the market to be spared; she was granted the surname Buliugu.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhao's Yuan empress was Man's daughter. She pleaded bitterly and bought herself back from the market to be spared; she was granted the surname Buliugu.

literal: He died; posthumously made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

literal: Man's younger brother Zhao, styled Jingyong, held Attendant; with his elder brother Cha he was executed at the same time.
idiomatic: Man's younger brother Zhao, styled Jingyong, held Attendant; with his elder brother Cha he was executed at the same time.

literal: Ji's younger brother Luohou, at the move to Luoyang, because the tombs were in the north settled his household in Changping commandery of Yan Province.
idiomatic: Ji's younger brother Luohou, at the move to Luoyang, because the tombs were in the north settled his household in Changping commandery of Yan Province.

literal: Rich within, he did only as he pleased.
idiomatic: Rich within, he did only as he pleased.

literal: He did not enter the capital; among guests who came and went he always gave lavish gifts and held great renown in the north.
idiomatic: He did not enter the capital. Among guests who came and went he always gave lavish gifts and held great renown in the north.

literal: Because Cha held power he especially disliked entering office and accepted appointment as Governor of Changping alone.
idiomatic: Because Cha held power he especially disliked entering office and accepted appointment as Governor of Changping alone.

literal: Emperor Mingyuan had seven sons: the Du Secret Empress bore Emperor Taiwu;
idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan had seven sons. The Du Secret Empress bore Emperor Taiwu;

literal: the Great Consort Murong bore Prince of Leping Li Pi;
idiomatic: the Great Consort Murong bore the Prince of Leping Li, Pi;

literal: Prince of Anding Mi—the mother's name is unknown;
idiomatic: the Prince of Anding Mi—the mother's name is unknown;

literal: Consort Murong bore Prince of Le'an Xuan Fan;
idiomatic: Consort Murong bore the Prince of Le'an Xuan, Fan;

literal: Consort Yin bore Prince of Yongchang Zhuang Jian;
idiomatic: Consort Yin bore the Prince of Yongchang Zhuang, Jian;

literal: Prince of Jianning Chong and Prince of Xinxing Jun—both mothers unknown.
idiomatic: the Prince of Jianning Chong and the Prince of Xinxing Jun—both mothers unknown.
